report.tagline: A platform where writers and video creators publish newsletters and charge readers a monthly subscription, with Substack taking 10%.
report.simpleSummary: Substack lets anyone start a newsletter that lands in readers' email inbox and in the Substack app. Writers can keep it free or charge, say $8 a month, for paid posts, and Substack keeps 10% of what readers pay. Readers find new writers through recommendations from writers they already read, so popular writers help grow each other. Famous journalists, historians and podcasters now run whole businesses on it.

overview.whatItDoes: Substack gives writers, podcasters and video makers a free tool to publish and get paid by subscribers. It handles email delivery, a website, payments and an app. Readers get a single app to read, listen to and chat with all the creators they follow.
howItWorks: A writer signs up for free, names a publication and starts posting.
Readers subscribe with their email; posts arrive by email and in the Substack app.
The writer turns on paid subscriptions at a price they choose, often $5 to $10 a month or $50 to $100 a year.
Substack keeps 10% and Stripe takes about 3% for card processing; the writer keeps the rest and owns the email list.
Writers recommend other publications; new subscribers see those recommendations when they sign up.
Notes (a short-post feed), Chat, live video and podcasts keep readers inside the app.
overview.valueProposition: For creators: a free way to earn directly from readers, keep your audience and avoid algorithms and ads. For readers: support writers you like and get their best work in one place.

businessModel.summary: Substack makes money mainly from one thing: 10% of every paid subscription. It does not run ads. Its revenue grows only when writers earn more, so it focuses on helping writers get more paying readers.

revenueStreams.detail: The main revenue. Stripe fees are paid by the writer on top.
Readers can pay in the iOS app; Substack passes on app store costs through higher in-app prices.
Readers can pay more as founding members; still 10% cut.

businessModel.pricing: Free for creators. Substack takes 10% of paid subscription revenue, plus Stripe card fees of about 2.9% + $0.30 per payment. Writers set prices, minimum about $5 a month.
costDrivers: Email delivery to tens of millions of inboxes
Engineering for the app, video and live
Advances and deals paid to win big writers (Substack Pro, used in early years)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a reader paying $80 a year. Substack keeps $8, Stripe takes about $2.60, and the writer keeps about $69. Sending emails and hosting cost Substack well under $1 per reader per year, so most of the $8 is margin before staff costs. Free readers cost little but earn nothing. Substack needs many writers with many paid readers, and its take rate (the share it keeps) is 10%.

howTheyGetUsers: Famous writers and journalists bring their audiences
Links shared on X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp
growth.moat: Recommendations create a network effect. Writers grow by being on Substack, and readers have all subscriptions in one app. Rivals like Beehiiv and Ghost charge less but lack this network.

improvementIdeas.idea: Reader bundles: pay one price, for example $25 a month, to read up to five chosen paid newsletters, with revenue split by reading time
improvementIdeas.problem: Subscription fatigue: readers stop at two or three paid newsletters.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More readers pay, and mid-sized writers get paid readers they would not win alone.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Paid subscriptions per paying reader and total paid subscriptions

improvementIdeas.idea: Lower take rate tiers, such as 7% above $1 million a year in reader payments
improvementIdeas.problem: Top writers leave for flat-fee tools to save money.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Keeps big writers, who bring audiences that help everyone through recommendations.

improvementIdeas.idea: Rupee pricing with UPI and UPI AutoPay for Indian readers
improvementIdeas.problem: Indian readers rarely pay dollar prices by card, so Indian writers struggle to earn.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher free-to-paid conversion in India and more Indian writers.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Paid conversion rate among Indian readers

improvementIdeas.idea: Topic pages that rank publications by reader retention, not just size
improvementIdeas.problem: New writers are hard to find, and big names dominate the feed.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better discovery for good small writers and more subscriptions per app visit.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Subscriptions from discovery per weekly app reader

pmLessons: Align your revenue with your customers' success. Substack only earns when writers earn, which makes writers trust it.
A network effect can come from creators helping each other, not just users inviting friends. Recommendations turned single newsletters into a network.
A percentage cut feels fair when creators are small but painful when they are big. Plan pricing for your best customers early.
Moving readers from email to your own app gives you control, but you must make the app better than the inbox.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase free-to-paid conversion on Substack?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the funnel from free reader to payer. Find the biggest drop (paywall views, checkout, trials). Propose 2 tests, such as timed trials or better paywall placement, with conversion as the metric and unsubscribes as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Substack lower its 10% take rate?
interviewQuestions.hint: Estimate revenue lost vs writers kept. Segment writers by earnings. Consider tiered rates or extra paid tools instead. Name the metric you would watch: top writer retention.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Substack's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Argue for active paid subscriptions, since each one is a reader valuing a writer. Break it into active writers, free readers, conversion and retention.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Substack in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at supply (Indian writers, regional languages) and demand (readers' willingness to pay). Fix payments (UPI, rupee pricing), then pick a pilot niche like personal finance.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain how recommendations create a network effect on Substack.
interviewQuestions.hint: Draw the loop: writer A recommends B, B gains readers, B recommends A back, both grow. Show why a new rival cannot copy this without many writers.

assumptions: Substack's own revenue of $45 million to $60 million is estimated from 10% of reader payments; the company does not publish revenue.
Paid subscriptions are likely above 5 million by late 2026, but no newer official number was found.
Difficulty of payouts and payments for Indian writers and readers is inferred from Stripe's limited India support.
Typical prices of $5 to $10 a month are common examples, not an official average.
